A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HEIST study. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original clinical prediction, cell annotation, gene imputation, clustering, runtime and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, a no-pretraining ablation and silhouette scores.

M1.justification: v2 Section 2.2 adds the positive-pair exponential to each of the three contrastive-loss denominators shown in v1 Section 3.2. This revises the specified objective; the architecture, graph construction, message passing and decoder remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether implementation or training changed.

E1.justification: The pretraining corpus and downstream SEA-AD, MERFISH lung, Charville, UPMC, DFCI, melanoma and placenta coverage are retained. v2 explicitly identifies the already-used CODEX/MIBI datasets as proteomics. Table A2's dataset counts and task assignments are unchanged despite revised organ-count summaries in the prose.

E2.justification: v2 adds Novae to clinical prediction and cell annotation comparisons, reporting scores or insufficient-marker failures, and adds MAGIC as an imputation comparator rather than solely a preprocessing component. These additions broaden substantive comparisons across three core tasks. Figure 3 also removes the raw gene-expression reference panel; the existing learned baselines remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds explicit aligned-marker evaluations for CellPLM and scGPT-spatial, a no-pretraining control, and silhouette scoring. The described UPMC marker count changes from 40 to 28, without establishing a dataset change or rerun. Main training settings, downstream task metrics and stated splitting procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a no-pretraining ablation across clinical prediction, imputation and annotation. Figure 3 revises the L4-IT neighborhood analysis from four displayed associated clusters to three subclusters and adds silhouette comparisons. Existing component ablations, the positional-encoding ablation and Appendix Figure A2 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state five repetitions with mean and standard deviation, retaining the same Charville/UPMC split qualification. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds Novae and aligned-baseline results, MAGIC correlations of 0.749/0.671 for placenta/skin, no-pretraining results, and silhouette scores of 0.17/0.26/0.29 for CellPLM/scGPT-spatial/HEIST. HEIST's UPMC/DFCI annotation scores remain 0.2826/0.1124, while reported comparative margins fall from 311.3%/81.9% to 28.7%/17.9% with expanded comparisons. v2 Table 2 apparently misassigns GraphST's retained numerical sequence after reordering columns, changing its reported placenta score from 0.644 to 0.659. Most original HEIST and appendix scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The contrastive-loss definitions receive a substantive normalization revision through inclusion of positive-pair terms, and the aggregate loss has more explicit summation grouping. This is a limited mathematical revision; no theorem or proof is added, and the remaining architectural and positional-encoding mathematics is retained.

C1.justification: The core framing narrows gene-regulatory-network claims to co-expression modeling and makes transcriptomics-to-proteomics transfer without retraining explicit in the abstract and contributions. The hierarchical foundation-model contribution, pretraining scale, four downstream tasks and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes improvements over MAGIC to contextual cross-attention, interprets pretraining as especially useful for skewed clinical labels, and discusses residual marker limitations after alignment. The main temporal, causal and computational limitations persist. v1 Appendix F's explicit requirement for experimental validation before clinical translation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 changes the anonymous repository identifier from HEIST-908D to HEIST-E3F8 and adds a reproducibility statement describing configurations, preprocessing/training/evaluation scripts and supplementary dataset details. Their external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Hardware and Table A1 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Novae, MIBI and the transformer-as-GNN perspective, removes several regulatory and spatial-context references, and sharpens positioning around sparse co-expression graphs versus fully connected transformers. Most related-work coverage is retained after relocation to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around spatial omics and proteomics transfer. Related work moves to the appendix, graph construction gains a main-text explanation, positional-encoding material moves into the appendix, and results are reordered. New ethics and reproducibility sections accompany removal of the broader-impact section and widespread terminology revisions.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, typography and headers. Figure 3 is substantially redesigned with a focused subcluster display, neighborhood pie charts and a silhouette panel replacing the earlier arrangement. Comparison tables gain rows, reordered dataset columns and transcriptomics/proteomics separators; several displays move, while Appendix Figure A2 is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added Novae/MAGIC comparisons, marker-alignment evaluations and no-pretraining control make transfer and pretraining claims easier to assess, while co-expression terminology better matches the documented construction. Most HEIST scores remain unchanged. These gains are tempered by the apparent GraphST column misassignment in v2 Table 2 and removal of the explicit clinical-validation caveat, yielding a limited overall improvement.
